## Functions

### `realmForgeOperatorSwitchPending(desktop)`

Shell-private admission fence; it never retires an existing mount or scope.

### `retireRealmForgeOperatorSwitch(desktop)`

Existing shell retirement must not wait for an unfinished app mount.

### `async prepareRealmForgeOperatorSwitch(desktop, scope)`

Ordinary requested profile switching only, before OperatorContext revocation. Hold new RealmForge launches even when no process exists, then drain the exact original ready class through Desktop's existing graceful close. Dirty/form decisions refuse this request; Save/Discard/Cancel require a separate retry. The caller holds the returned release across other document preparation. At revocation, existing non-active/frozen launch checks replace this fence. A later failure does not reopen an already closed clean app. Raw lock/switch, emergency termination and other profile mutations are unchanged.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
